column1: # W2.2 frontier walk plan — THE plan, against the mainline frontend.
# Re-pinned 2026-08-20 (audit fix round) onto `main` @ 7ca8908e, which carries
# the merged bug-fix arc.  Before that merge there were TWO plans: a "pre-merge"
# one (71 action rows, because a method with an unlowerable body blocked the
# WHOLE export) and a "post-merge" one written against H-3.  H-3 landed as
# c7938b25, so the post-merge plan is simply the plan now and the pre-merge one
# is retired per handoff H-16.  What it measured is preserved as a NUMBER in
# docs/raft-w3-log.md §2.2 rather than as a file: 71 action rows vs 14, the
# difference being 35 method-body replacements + 22 further import drops, all
# artefacts of the missing per-declaration quarantine.
# file
# The last row is the terminal `*` row: it asserts the walk is COMPLETE.
# frontier.py refuses a plan without it and re-checks the final state in its
# exit code, so a truncated plan fails instead of reporting a shorter frontier.
# Nothing in the subject tree blocks the export except the EXPORT-BLOCKING gaps
# below, none of which a per-declaration quarantine can catch — an import
# refuses before any declaration is read, and a package-level variable has no
# body to replace with a refusing stub.
# Every row here is a PROBE DELTA standing in for a recorded gap
# (docs/raft-w3-log.md §3, the probe-delta ledger).  The subject tree keeps
# upstream's text; only the walk's work copy is touched.
# READ THE EXPECTATIONS AS "WHAT THE FRONTEND SAID AT THAT STEP", not as the
# cause of that declaration's refusal: the frontend reports ONE refusal at a
# time (JC-9).  The per-declaration causes are the CENSUS's job, and the census
# is taken off the wire by sweep.py after this walk reaches a clean export.
# G-1  the election-jitter seam.  raft's randomized election timeout draws from
#      crypto/rand + math/big inside (*lockedRand).Intn (raft.go:97).  The
#      refusal recorded here is NOT the draw: it is the transitive stdlib
#      closure of crypto/rand reaching crypto/internal/entropy/v1.0.0, whose
#      ESCAPED linker prefix the init graph re-escapes and then cannot find in
#      the inittask table (H-9, a frontend defect, minimised to a 6-line
#      2-package program — see the log).
#      THIS ROW MASKS A LIVE GAP, and the masking is the reason G-1 is two rows
#      in the census and not one.  Replacing Intn's body is forced — the body
#      cannot type-check once the imports H-9 refuses on are dropped — so the
#      draw's own refusal never reaches this wire.  sweep.py censuses it
#      separately, in a SINGLE-package probe where H-9 does not fire
#      (specInitOrder returns early below two units), and reports it beside the
#      walk's own numbers.  Any future probe delta that replaces a BODY owes
#      the same treatment.
raft/raft.go
# G-2/G-3  errors.New is unmodeled (G-2), and a package-level variable has no
#      per-declaration quarantine (G-3), so each of the NINE `var Err… =
#      errors.New(…)` initializers refuses the whole export.  G-3 is an
#      ALTERNATIVE route past G-2's globals, not an independent export blocker:
#      fix either one and these nine rows go away, which is why the log counts
#      TWO measured export-blocking gaps and not three.  The probe file
#      supplies Go's own implementation of errors.New under another name; the
#      errors.New calls inside function BODIES are deliberately left alone, so
#      the quarantine census still reports what G-2 costs.
raft/probe_errors_new.go
